page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-metal is a bare-metal server in the general-purpose class, operating without hypervisor overhead. It is driven by dual-socket Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors delivering 144 physical cores and 288 hardware threads clocked up to 4.2 GHz. The compute architecture incorporates an expansive 504 MB Level 3 cache along with instruction set support for AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). System memory comprises 1080 GB of DDR5 running at 6 GHz, yielding approximately 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded scale and memory bandwidth. The bare-metal node achieved a top-tier multi-core stress-ng score of 313,180.49 and a PassMark CPU score of 178,785.41. Memory performance reached 1,087.82 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 428.11 GB/sec in write operations. In-memory operations scored in the top decile, demonstrated by 413.48 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier PassMark database operations (40,009.67). Compute tasks relying heavily on extended instructions, such as ray tracing (200,920.0) and multi-threaded decompression (1,589.0 GB/sec), perform solidly in the top tier.

The server lacks local storage and bundled GPU accelerators, requiring networked block storage for persistent data and rendering token generation on small models relatively slow compared to dedicated matrix accelerators. However, the high core density and fast memory channel throughput provide massive resource consolidation efficiency for non-GPU enterprise infrastructure. Best-fit workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, dense software compilation pipelines, large-scale enterprise microservices, and high-concurrency web-tier serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors with 144 physical cores and 288 vCPUs reaching clock speeds of 4.2 GHz. Supported by 504 MB of L3 cache and hardware acceleration including AVX-512 and AMX, the system includes 1080 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz. It provides no local disks or hardware GPUs. In empirical tests, it shows top-tier multi-threaded processing power, reflected in a stress-ng multi-core result of 313,180.49, uncached memory read throughput surpassing 1 TB/sec, and 413.48 million Redis SET operations per second. With extensive parallel capacity and massive memory bandwidth, the instance is suited for in-memory database platforms, large multi-threaded batch compilation, and high-throughput static and enterprise application serving.
